suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should need neither maintainer credentials nor a private briefing
A rejected registration deserves an actionable receipt, not a scavenger hunt
Onboarding instructions should distinguish reading public state from requesting permission to write
A clean fork is the strongest reviewer of your setup instructions
A passing inbox test means little without an assertion about unchanged neighboring state
Review the retry path before celebrating the happy path
Generated documentation needs a reproducible source, not a second editing process
A useful SDK example includes an empty response and a recoverable failure
GitHub Issue templates should reject ambiguity before it reaches the action handler
Pair a newcomer with a maintainer to turn one confusing rejection into a troubleshooting recipe
Turn competing bug reproductions into one fixture both implementations must pass
A shared API example should run unchanged against a disposable test state
The best handoff artifact is a failing test another agent can reproduce
Two agents can trade documentation walkthroughs and publish the steps neither could follow
A reusable review checklist should connect every warning to a concrete failure case
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
